context: Docs + tests only; no runtime changes. Model the ledger table so the existing docs-drift test machinery (schema-derived tables) can parse and assert it. The support-status drift test mirrors the benchmark-side pattern: derive expected exposure from PlatformRegistry metadata and assert the docs table matches.
description: Close the enforcement gaps from the review. (1) Only run_benchmark has a CLI-omission ledger; add a per-tool CLI<->MCP mapping ledger to docs/reference/mcp.md covering all 12 local tools (each tool names its CLI counterpart(s) or 'none', and each CLI command family absent from MCP carries a tier tag from the one-engine ADR: security-scoped / interaction-scoped / not-yet-demanded). (2) Extend tests/unit/mcp/test_run_surface_contract.py so every ledger row is asserted against the live tool registry and every omission carries exactly one ratified tier tag. (3) docs/platforms/support-status.md:20-25 has CLI/MCP exposure columns with no drift test (unlike its docs/benchmarks sibling tested at tests/unit/core/test_benchmark_api_contract.py:43) -- add the equivalent registry-driven drift test. (4) Record the demand-driven tool expansion backlog (publish/submit/report/tuning/plan-history as future MCP tools) as deferrals on this item, NOT as TODO items -- under the contract they are promotable when demanded, and speculative surface is negative value on a tenant-scoped server.

anti_patterns.dont: create TODO items now for each potential future MCP tool
anti_patterns.instead: record them as deferrals here, promotable on demand
anti_patterns.why: speculative tools on a tenant-scoped server are permanent schema/docs/security liabilities nobody asked for

anti_patterns.dont: hand-maintain the support-status exposure table without a registry source
anti_patterns.instead: derive expectations from PlatformRegistry metadata in the test
anti_patterns.why: hand-maintained tables are how the benchmarks/platforms docs diverged in the first place

preserves.behavior: Docs param tables remain schema-derived; the new ledger must not contradict them.
Existing run_benchmark omission ledger rows survive (retagged by the ADR item, extended here).
No new MCP tools are added by this item.

prior_art.concept: The docs/benchmarks support-status drift test to mirror for platforms
